_about: The starter dictionary for bendit's controlled vocabulary: one word, one meaning.
Modelled on ASD-STE100, Section 1. This file is DATA. To grow it, run `--init` to copy
it to <repo>/.claude/vocabulary.json and edit the copy; do not edit the script to change
policy. A repo-local file REPLACES this one, so keep the terms you still want.
Rules: `substitute` (exact one-for-one swaps, safe for --fix), `obligation` (a modal
aimed at the agent, instruction files only), `evidence` (a completion claim naming no
observation, report files only). Each term is {"use": replacement, "why": reason}.
Add a term only when you can name what it should say instead, and delete one that
fires more than it catches: a rule that cries wolf gets switched off.

substitute._why: ASD-STE100 panel D. Exact one-for-one swaps with no judgment required. Safe to auto-fix.

utilize.why: register inflation; no meaning is added

utilise.why: register inflation; no meaning is added

prior to.why: STE Section 1: BEFORE is the approved form

subsequent to.why: STE Section 1: AFTER is the approved form

commence.why: STE Section 1: START is the approved form

approximately.why: STE Section 1: ABOUT is the approved form

a number of.why: hides whether the count is known

it is imperative that.why: names no actor; STE requires an actor

obligation._why: STE Section 7 requires an unambiguous instruction. A modal addressed to the agent turns a requirement into a suggestion, and the agent takes the suggestion. Only agent-directed modals are flagged; 'a principal that should be denied' describes an expectation and is correct.

should.why: a requirement stated as advice is followed about half the time

try to.why: unfalsifiable: there is no observation that shows it was not tried

where possible.use: name when it is not possible
where possible.why: the agent decides it was not possible

if possible.use: name when it is not possible
if possible.why: the agent decides it was not possible

as appropriate.why: the agent decides what is appropriate

_why: A claim that work is done asserts rung 4 or 5 of the evidence ladder (1 said so, 2 pointed
at the line, 3 showed the bad case cannot happen, 4 ran it and read the output, 5
reproduced it in the running app). This fires when such a claim names no observation: no
rung, no command, no exit code, no file:line, no artifact path, within three lines.
It is aimed at REPORT prose (progress notes, PR bodies, verification writeups), not at
instruction prose, which legitimately discusses these words.

validated.use: name the run and its output

tested.use: name the scenario and the verdict

it works.use: name the run and its output

works as expected.use: name the expectation and the observation

should be fine.use: name what you checked, or say you did not
should be fine.why: a guess stated as a result

looks good.why: a guess stated as a result

successfully.use: delete it, or name the success signal
